source: The Vegetarian Society of the United Kingdom, "Seasonal UK Grown Produce" (blog page, published 1 January 2022)
license: facts transcribed, page is copyright of publisher (The Vegetarian Society of the United Kingdom Limited)
semantics: Page lists UK-grown produce "in season" per month as plain comma-separated text under one h2 heading per month. No distinction between freshly harvested and stored produce; winter listings of apples, pears, onions, potatoes, squash etc. implicitly include stored produce.
method: Fetched the single HTML page with curl, stripped script/style, split on the twelve <h2> month headings, tag-stripped and split each month paragraph on commas. Built a 12-boolean vector per distinct name (true if listed under that month). Spelling variants merged into one item (Parsnip -> Parsnips, Swish Chard -> Swiss Chard, Courgette -> Courgettes, Swede -> Swedes) with the variant noted. name_en assigned by hand mapping using the shared cross-region convention.
name_en_convention: US/international names for the joinable key: eggplant, zucchini, beetroot, sweetcorn, swede, rocket, spring onion, snow pea, sweet pepper, chili pepper.
caveats: Single-source editorial list, not an official statistic.
Includes a few foraged/non-produce items (Elderflowers, Elderberries, Chestnuts, Samphire, Wild Mushrooms, Morel Mushrooms) flagged in notes.
Some month lists are visibly incomplete relative to others (e.g. Carrots absent in May/June, Onions absent Mar-Jun), so "false" means "not listed", not "definitely unavailable".
